subject.title: [Bug] Gateway swallows user-visible reply when an agent's exec stdout matches "configuration file" — replies=2 puts ⚠️ 🛠️ first, the actual reply second

question: For a successful agent turn with an ambiguous or recovered exec signal, should OpenClaw suppress the user-visible warning by default unless structured evidence confirms an actionable failed mutation?
rationale: The remaining behavior is cross-channel product policy: it balances preventing misleading warnings against preserving visibility for genuine tool failures.

options.title: Require confirmed actionable failure
options.body: Emit a user-visible warning only when structured tool state confirms a failed action that needs user attention; ignore stdout-derived or recovered ambiguity.

options.title: Keep warnings but demote them
options.body: Retain ambiguous tool diagnostics after the answer with clearly non-fatal presentation, accepting continued user-facing noise.

options.title: Scope to Feishu presentation only
options.body: Change only Feishu ordering or rendering while retaining the shared warning policy, leaving other channels unchanged.

recommendation.title: Require confirmed actionable failure
recommendation.body: Emit a user-visible warning only when structured tool state confirms a failed action that needs user attention; ignore stdout-derived or recovered ambiguity.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the Feishu final-payload boundary and provides the clearest routing point for the cross-channel warning-policy decision.
